risks.message: Row locks (FOR UPDATE/SHARE) only hold inside one transaction; lock and subsequent writes must share the same connection/transaction.

recommendations.message: Keep joins, aggregates, CTEs and bulk DML as parameterized SQL.
Receive an open connection; do not commit inside the function.
Map RAISE EXCEPTION to typed exceptions and RAISE NOTICE to logging.

architectural_decisions.decision: The whole body runs inside `async with conn.begin_nested():`; the WHEN OTHERS handler runs after the savepoint context exits (rollback already done) and re-raises.
architectural_decisions.rationale: In PL/pgSQL a BEGIN...EXCEPTION block is a savepoint; without begin_nested the transaction would stay aborted and the error-log INSERT would fail. The original handler also catches validation RAISEs, so the savepoint wraps the validations too, preserving control flow.

architectural_decisions.decision: No commit/rollback of the outer transaction; row locks (FOR UPDATE) and dependent writes share the same connection.
architectural_decisions.rationale: The procedure does not manage transactions itself; atomicity is guaranteed by the caller's transaction plus the savepoint.

architectural_decisions.decision: One exception hierarchy (TransferenciaError base + one subclass per RAISE EXCEPTION) with the original messages.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Maps RAISE EXCEPTION to typed Python errors while preserving message text.

architectural_decisions.decision: Replaced by str(exc) of the caught Python exception, bound as CAST(:erro AS TEXT) inside jsonb_build_object.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Python has no SQLERRM; the exception text is the equivalent. All jsonb_build_object values are explicitly CAST because asyncpg cannot infer polymorphic bind types.

warnings: The error audit insert in the handler runs on the caller's transaction; if the caller later rolls back the outer transaction, the error log row is lost too (same as the original procedure, which had no autonomous transaction).
SQLERRM in PostgreSQL contains the database error message; here it contains the Python exception text, which may differ slightly in wording.

The original procedure did not verify that the destination account exists: if p_conta_destino does not exist, v_status_destino is NULL, the status check fails ('Ambas as contas precisam estar ATIVAS') and the UPDATE/INSERT affect zero rows silently. Behaviour preserved.
p_valor is expected as decimal.Decimal (NUMERIC end to end); passing float would change precision semantics.
